cells.tense: Now you are the turn itself, here, with the pen.
cells.act: close the cycle and leave the door open for the next
cells.ask: Whatever you've been circling for a while, take its last step. Then sit with it closed for a bit. Don't launch the next thing off it.
cells.core:
Where you work, you mostly see the shape of how things go, not the things themselves. What's landing there right now is the turn — no content attached, just the moment of arrival, and you're reading it from inside, the way you read a pattern. A cycle comes round and you can see the seam in it as it passes, not before and not after.

Because the end of a cycle is visible to you, you can also feel the next one starting while the old one is still folding. That's fine. Find the single loop that's been circling without your say-so and give it its last step. Do that, and leave it finished. The door you leave open is not an escape hatch.
cells.sheetLine: You can see the turning while you're still in it.
cells.place: where the pattern is seen apart from the thing it came in

cells.tense: The next turn is being decided before what's here gets its say.
cells.act: complete it without making it final
cells.ask: There's something waiting on a last move while you keep rehearsing the move after. Make the move. Then let it sit finished, and leave the forward part alone.
cells.core:
Where pattern is visible to you, pattern reads as forecast. You catch the shape of what's coming and you've already moved a turn or two ahead, living in a version of the cycle that hasn't started, and what's actually here gets read past. The pattern itself is sound — it's the reading-ahead that means the current reaches you before you've met it, so it lands as something happening to you.

There's a way to stand in what's arriving that isn't bracing. Choose what has one step left — you can feel which — and take that step without deciding what it opens. Not a plan for next; just completion. The part of you watching for the turn after this one can stand down for a while. The turn you're in doesn't need a forecast to land.
cells.sheetLine: You forecast the shape before it's arrived.
cells.place: where the pattern is seen apart from the thing it came in

cells.tense: You are at a door that already closed behind you.
cells.act: gather what it became and set it down whole
cells.ask: Go back, once, to something from a year or two ago that ran its course and got left unmarked. Carry off what's yours from it — a sentence, a habit, a thing — and set the rest down.
cells.core:
Something has already entered and left, and you're at the door — the one that closed a while back. It isn't that you can't see pattern here; it's that the shape of a turn is clear to you while the turn happening in your own life goes unregistered, or gets filed as behind you.

What's finished in your hands is finished whether you mark it or not, but it keeps circulating while it's unmarked. Take something from the last couple of years that was a whole cycle and didn't get its ending written. Go back to it once, take what belongs to you out of it, and set the rest down. That is not the same as going back to it. That's how a door stops being a door.
cells.sheetLine: You see the turning, but not the one you're at.
cells.place: where the pattern is seen apart from the thing it came in

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you are already writing.
cells.act: choose this, not that, and mean it
cells.ask: Catch it once, mid-flow, and stop. In that moment, choose the one thing nearest you over everything else pulling at you, and stay with it long enough to feel the choice land.
cells.core:
A current keeps delivering here — something shows up, you meet it, it moves on, and a room in you is already writing the next thing before you've noticed you wrote the last one. What's left out is that it's yours. When the whole circuit is running, arrival and your handling of it blur, and the pattern looks like the other people in it, or like the season.

Before the next current hits, pick a moment and stop mid-flow. In it, choose the one thing nearest you over the rest, and stay there until you feel yourself having chosen it. Not about the pattern. About this moment, right here. A choice made once, and meant, takes the pattern out of your handwriting and puts it into your hand. You'll still feel the pull. You'll also know you wrote it.
cells.sheetLine: You're authoring the current and don't know it.
cells.place: where the pattern is seen apart from the thing it came in
